summary: Amazon CloudFront now supports AWS Service Quotas, so you can view, monitor, and request increases for 28 CloudFront quotas from the Service Quotas console or API. Until now, increasing a quota on resources such as distributions, cache policies, origins, or alternate domain names meant opening a support case and waiting for manual review. If you have AWS Business Support or higher, requests for limit increases within published thresholds are now approved automatically. For example, you can raise your distribution quota from 500 to 1,000, or the number of alternate domain names per distribution from 100 to 500, without opening a support case. Some quotas also publish usage metrics to Amazon CloudWatch every 5 minutes, so you can set alarms and request an increase before you reach a limit.. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon CloudFront is supported. To get started, visit the Service Quotas console to view and request increases for your CloudFront quotas. To learn more, see Amazon CloudFront quotas in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide.
title: Amazon CloudFront now supports self-service increases in AWS Service Quotas

summary: Amazon Textract is now available in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich) Regions. Amazon Textract is a machine learning service that automatically extracts text, handwriting, and data from scanned documents, going beyond simple optical character recognition (OCR) to identify and extract text and structured data. At launch in these Regions, Amazon Textract supports text detection and document analysis. This includes the DetectDocumentText, AnalyzeDocument, StartDocumentTextDetection, GetDocumentTextDetection, StartDocumentAnalysis, and GetDocumentAnalysis operations. The AnalyzeExpense, AnalyzeID, and AnalyzeLending operations, and Custom Queries (adapters), are not available in these Regions at this time. With this launch, Amazon Textract is available in a total of 18 AWS Regions: US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), Europe (Spain), the AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West) Regions, and the newly added Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich) Regions. To learn more, see the Amazon Textract product page and the Amazon Textract Developer Guide . For pricing and Region availability, see the Amazon Textract pricing page and Amazon Textract endpoints and quotas .
title: Amazon Textract now available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich)

summary: Amazon Textract now provides an updated text detection model that improves accuracy, expands language support, and enhances multilingual table extraction. The updated model applies to the DetectDocumentText and AnalyzeDocument APIs and requires no changes to your Amazon Textract API requests or response schema. Your applications are served by the updated model automatically, so you can continue calling Amazon Textract exactly as before. The updated model expands language coverage to more than 40 languages, including Albanian, Arabic, Basque, Belarusian, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latvian, Lithuanian, Luxembourgish, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Serbian Cyrillic, Serbian Latin, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Turkmen, and Ukrainian, enabling reliable processing of previously unsupported scripts. Accuracy improvements include enhanced long-word recognition and handwriting detection. Additionally, multilingual table extraction is more robust on merged cells, skewed or rotated tables, and partial or corrupted tables. These improvements help you accurately process invoices, forms, identity documents, and other multilingual or complex documents, including those with tables, at scale. The updated Amazon Textract model is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Textract is availab
title: Announcing an updated text detection model for Amazon Textract

summary: Amazon Inspector now extends its vulnerability scanning to EC2 Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), enabling you to identify software vulnerabilities in your AMIs without launching instances or installing additional software. This helps you fix issues at the source before AMIs are used to launch instances across your fleet. With this capability, you can run continuous evaluations to monitor your AMI catalog for newly discovered vulnerabilities, or perform targeted one-time scans for specific AMIs directly from the EC2 Console. You can enable AMI scanning for an account or across your entire organization in Amazon Inspector. For AWS Security Hub customers, you can enable AMI scanning as an add-on across your organization, and findings are also delivered to Security Hub. Based on the scan results, you can enable the Allowed AMIs setting and specify security criteria that AMIs must meet to be available within your account and enforce this setting across the entire organization using Declarative Policies. Customers building AMIs with EC2 Image Builder can integrate scanning directly into their pipelines and restrict distribution of AMIs that do not meet their security standards. AMI Scanning helps you detect and remediate vulnerabilities earlier in your deployment pipeline, reducing the risk of deploying compromised compute resources. Security teams can now establish a consistent vulnerability scanning process across all AMIs improving their security posture before instances are launche
title: EC2 Amazon Machine Images can now be scanned for vulnerabilities through Amazon Inspector

summary: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Cases and External Tool events in the Wait block, giving you more control over how your customer experience flows react to real-time data changes. In addition to waiting for a Lambda function to complete, you can now wait until a Connect Case field meets a specified condition or an External Tool invocation completes. This enables you to wait for critical information before advancing an interaction, reducing unnecessary transfers and saving time for both your end-customers and agents. For example, you can hold a flow until a refund status field is updated on a case, then automatically resume and route the interaction based on the outcome. To learn more about this feature, refer to the administrator guide and availability of Connect Customer features by Region . To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.
title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Cases and External Tool events in the Wait block

summary: Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to invoke Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in customer experience flows through the new 'External Tool' block. With this launch, you can connect flows to third-party applications through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and reuse the same tools used by your agentic experiences to retrieve data or trigger actions, without writing custom Lambda functions. For example, when a customer contacts a financial institution about a recent transaction, a flow can use the External Tool block to retrieve relevant context from a third-party application, such as case history from their CRM system, or transaction details from a banking platform. This feature is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). To learn more about this feature, refer to the administrator guide . To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.
title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in flows

summary: Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 3 (compatible with MySQL 8.0) supports MySQL 8.0.46, which includes community MySQL fixes and Aurora-specific improvements. In addition to operational improvements, Aurora MySQL 3.14 introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in-transit. For detailed information on this release, refer to Aurora MySQL 3 and MySQL 8.0.46 release notes. You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your clusters in phases. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Aurora MySQL is available. Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full MySQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at Aurora’s getting started page .
title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 3.14 (compatible with MySQL 8.0.46) is generally available

summary: Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 8.4 supports MySQL 8.4.10. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by the MySQL community. For more details, refer to the Aurora MySQL 8.4 and MySQL 8.4.10 release notes. Aurora MySQL 8.4.10 adds support for global transaction identifiers (GTID) tags, which lets you assign a user-defined tag to GTIDs to help you identify and group related transactions in binary log replication. This release also adds support for a maximum of 50,000 simultaneous connections per DB instance, which allows connection-intensive applications to scale without adding a connection pooling layer. Learn more about maximum connections best practices in the Amazon Aurora MySQL User Guide . You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your clusters in phases, validating on lower-priority environments before upgrading your most critical ones. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon Aurora User Guide . This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Aurora MySQL
title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 8.4.10 is now generally available

summary: AWS Lambda now supports queues for Apache Kafka in self-managed Kafka event source mappings (ESM), for Kafka clusters that customers run themselves and for managed offerings such as Confluent Cloud. Customers can now scale processing for Kafka workloads beyond the partition count of a topic, increasing throughput during traffic spikes and improving processing resilience. Customers building event-driven Kafka workloads for use cases such as image and video encoding, fraud detection, notification delivery, and telemetry ingestion treat each event as an independent unit of work, where processing speed matters more than strict ordering. Previously, Kafka ESMs used the Kafka consumer group protocol, which assigns each partition to exactly one consumer within a consumer group. Customers needing higher parallelism had to over-partition topics or move traffic to a separate queuing system, adding infrastructure to operate and producer code to maintain. Queue support for self-managed Kafka ESMs is built on Kafka share groups, which are generally available in Apache Kafka 4.2. This launch enables multiple event pollers to consume concurrently from the same partition, with each event poller supporting up to 10 concurrent invocations. This decouples parallelism from partition count with no changes to producers, topic configuration, or function code. As a result, customers get higher throughput during traffic spikes and more resilient processing, because a slow or failed event no longer ho
title: AWS Lambda now supports queues for Apache Kafka in self-managed Kafka event sources

summary: For organizations that use Amazon Quick, the desktop application now signs users in with the same sign-in method the organization already uses for Quick on the web. Administrators no longer need to register an OIDC application in their identity provider or set up separate desktop sign-in before users can get started. If a user can sign in to Quick on the web, that user can sign in to the desktop application. To turn on desktop access, an administrator adds the desktop connector once in the Amazon Quick console. Users then enter their Quick account name, choose Sign In, and finish signing in through their browser. This works for accounts that use IAM Identity Center, IAM federation, or native Amazon Quick users. If your organization wants to manage desktop sign-in separately, you can still set up a dedicated identity provider configuration with providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, or Ping Identity. Amazon Quick on desktop is available in AWS Regions that support the full Amazon Quick feature set . To get started, see Amazon Quick on desktop in the Amazon Quick User Guide.
title: Amazon Quick on desktop now uses your organization's existing Amazon Quick sign-in

summary: Starting today, Amazon RDS supports per snapshot billing for Amazon RDS snapshots. Per snapshot billing allows you to get the cost of each individual snapshot. Previously, RDS snapshot charges were aggregated at the database instance level on the Cost and Usage report as well as the Cost Explorer. This meant that while understanding the snapshot charges, you could only see the aggregate view at the database instance instead of drilling down to each individual snapshot. Now, you can use cost allocation tags on your snapshots to see exactly how much each snapshot costs, giving you a better understanding of your backups spend and budgets. Per snapshot billing is enabled by default on all RDS snapshots for no additional charge. Per snapshot billing is available for all Amazon RDS engines in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, please visit our documentation .
title: Amazon RDS now supports per snapshot billing

summary: A new Anthropic model is now available in the Kiro IDE and CLI for the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. With Haiku 5.5, all three Claude 5.5 models are now available in Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US). Claude Haiku 5.5 is the fastest model in the Claude 5.5 family. It's a clear step up from Claude Haiku 4.5, built for work that runs in large volumes and needs quick responses. Developers can use it to summarize and compact long context, classify and route requests, process text in bulk, and make small, targeted edits across many files. It also works well as a review subagent that runs in parallel, while Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 take on harder planning and coding work. Haiku 5.5 uses adaptive thinking across five effort levels from low to max, with medium as the default. It's available with a 1M context window and a 0.06x credit multiplier. Requests over 100K tokens are billed at a 0.3x multiplier. Ensure your IDE or CLI is updated to the latest version, then restart it to access the new model from the model selector. For more details, visit the GovCloud documentation , the monitoring and tracking guide , or contact your AWS account team. To learn more about Kiro, visit the Kiro product page .
title: Haiku 5.5 now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)

summary: AWS for Fluent Bit announces version 3.0.0 , based on Fluent Bit version 4.1.1 and Amazon Linux 2023. Container logging using AWS for Fluent Bit is now more performant and more feature-rich for AWS customers, including those using Amazon Elastic Container Services (Amazon ECS) and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). AWS for Fluent Bit enables Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS customers to collect, process, and route container logs to destinations including Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, and Amazon S3 without changing application code. AWS for Fluent Bit 3.0.0 upgrades the Fluent Bit version to 4.1.1, and upgrades the base image to Amazon Linux 2023. These updates deliver access to the latest Fluent Bit features, significant performance improvements, and enhanced security. New features include native OpenTelemetry (OTel) support for ingesting and forwarding OTLP logs, metrics, and traces with AWS SigV4 authentication. Performance improvements include faster JSON parsing, processing more logs per vCPU with lower latency. Security enhancements include TLS min version and cipher controls, which enforce your TLS policy on outputs from AWS for Fluent Bit for stronger protocol posture. You can use AWS for Fluent Bit 3.0.0 on both ECS and EKS. On ECS, update the FireLens log-router container image in your task definition to the 3.0.0 tag from the Amazon ECR Public Gallery. On EKS, upgrade by either updating the Helm release or setting t
title: Announcing AWS for Fluent Bit 3.0.0 based on Fluent Bit 4.1.1

summary: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now supports M8i and R8i instances in additional AWS Regions. Both M8i and R8i instances are now available in Asia Pacific (New Zealand) and Canada West (Calgary), and R8i instances are now available in Europe (Milan, Stockholm, and Zurich) and Israel (Tel Aviv). These instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors, available only on AWS, delivering the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. The M8i and R8i instances offer up to 15% better price-performance, and 2.5x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation Intel-based instances. M8i and R8i instances are available for Amazon RDS for Oracle in Bring Your Own License model for Oracle Database Enterprise Edition (EE) and Oracle Database Standard Edition 2 (SE2). For EE, instances are available in sizes from large to 48xlarge, as well as bare metal sizes metal-48xl and metal-96xl. For SE2, instances are available in sizes from large to 4xlarge and bare metal sizes metal-48xl and metal-96xl. Refer to Amazon RDS for Oracle Pricing for available instance configurations, pricing, and region availability.
title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports M8i and R8i instances in additional AWS Regions

summary: The Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Capability for Argo CD now supports Argo CD Notifications, providing notifications when your applications sync, fail, or change health. You define triggers and message templates in your cluster and subscribe individual Applications with an annotation, the same way you do in upstream Argo CD. With this launch, you can deliver notifications to 16 notification services, including Slack, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Amazon SQS, and Amazon EventBridge. The Amazon SQS and Amazon EventBridge services authenticate with your IAM Capability Role, so you can route deployment events into your own event-driven workflows without storing credentials in your cluster. For a service that requires third-party credentials such as a Slack token, you can specify an AWS Secrets Manager ARN in place of the secret and EKS will automatically use it on your behalf. Notifications are available in all AWS Regions where the EKS Capability for Argo CD is available, at no additional charge. Standard charges apply for resources related to the services your notifications use, for example Amazon SQS or Amazon EventBridge. To learn more, visit Amazon EKS and refer to the Amazon EKS User Guide .
title: Amazon EKS Capabilities now supports Argo CD Notifications

summary: AWS Transform for mainframe now discovers business functions with field-level precision and generates a new requirements coverage report in the assess and reimagine workflow. Previously, business functions that used the same table or file were grouped together, and you had to build your own traceability reporting from AWS Transform artifacts. With this launch, you can start modernizing z/OS COBOL and PL/I workloads from a more accurate catalog of business functions and verify requirements coverage before you build. Business functions are now grouped only when they affect the same data fields. They also include screens and queues and carry clearer names and descriptions. The new requirements coverage report shows how every part of your application is accounted for in the generated requirements. Every line of source code is classified by how it was handled, every business rule links to the exact lines it came from, and every requirement is backed by the business rules that support it. You can review coverage from the full portfolio down to a single line before moving into forward engineering in Kiro and other IDEs. These capabilities are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform for mainframe is available. For more information, see the AWS Region table . To learn more, visit AWS Transform for mainframe or see the AWS Transform for mainframe documentation .
title: AWS Transform for mainframe improves the reimagine modernization workflow

summary: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports the latest Cumulative Updates (CU) and General Distribution Release (GDR) updates for Microsoft SQL Server. This release includes support for Microsoft SQL Server 2017 CU31+GDR KB5128496 (RDS version 14.00.3560.2.v1), SQL Server 2019 CU32+GDR KB5128494 (RDS version 15.00.4500.2.v1), SQL Server 2022 CU27+GDR KB5126934 (RDS version 16.00.4305.5.v1) and SQL Server 2025 CU10 KB5125471 (RDS version 17.00.5035.5.v1). For additional information on the improvements and fixes included in these updates, see Microsoft documentation for KB5128496, KB5128494, KB5126934 and KB5125471. We recommend that you upgrade your Amazon RDS for SQL Server instances to apply these updates using Amazon RDS Management Console, or by using the AWS SDK or CLI. You can learn more about upgrading your database instance in the Amazon RDS SQL Server User Guide for upgrading your RDS Microsoft SQL Server DB engine .
title: Amazon RDS now supports the latest Cumulative Update and GDR updates for Microsoft SQL Server

summary: AWS Config now supports 10 additional AWS resource types across key services including Amazon ElastiCache and Amazon QuickSight. This expansion provides greater coverage over your AWS environment, enabling you to more effectively discover, assess, audit, and remediate an even broader range of resources. With this launch, if you have enabled recording for all resource types, then AWS Config will automatically track these new additions. The newly supported resource types are also available in Config rules and Config aggregators. You can now use AWS Config to monitor the following newly supported resource types in all AWS Regions where the resources are available: Resource Types: AWS::Billing::BillingView AWS::MPA::IdentitySource AWS::Connect::HoursOfOperation AWS::Notifications::OrganizationalUnitAssociation AWS::ElastiCache::CacheCluster AWS::NotificationsContacts::EmailContact AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup AWS::Oam::Link AWS::MediaLive::SignalMap AWS::QuickSight::Agent
title: AWS Config now supports 10 new resource types

summary: Amazon Connect Customer automatically fills in the customer’s email address from the linked customer profile when agents start a new email thread from a case. This saves agents time and reduces manual entry errors by eliminating the need to look up or type the address. Cases is available in the following AWS regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .
title: Amazon Connect Customer prefills the email address for new threads started from cases

summary: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents pause emails while waiting for information or approvals, freeing them to handle higher-priority contacts and resume their work later. For example, an agent waiting for a supervisor to approve a refund can pause the email and take an incoming call. Paused time is tracked separately from active handling time, giving supervisors a more accurate view of the time agents spend working on emails. Agents can pause and resume emails directly from the Agent Workspace or Contact Control Panel (CCP) and see how long each email has been paused. Supervisors can monitor paused emails and pause duration in real time, and use flows to automatically resume or transfer emails that remain paused beyond a configured threshold. Amazon Connect Customer email pause and resume is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London) regions . To learn more and get started, please refer to the help documentation or visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.
title: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents pause and resume emails

summary: Amazon CloudWatch now supports bearer token authentication, using API keys (bearer tokens), as an additional option for sending OpenTelemetry traces to the AWS X-Ray OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) traces endpoint. Any OTLP/HTTP client that can set an Authorization header, including the OpenTelemetry Collector and OpenTelemetry SDK exporters, can now authenticate with a bearer token instead of signing requests with AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4). This helps teams send traces from workloads that can't use the AWS SDK or short-term credentials, such as applications running on premises or in other clouds, CI/CD pipelines, and third-party tools that support only a static Authorization header. SigV4 remains the recommended authentication method for sending traces to CloudWatch, and the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) SDKs continue to use SigV4 by default with no changes required. Traces sent with either method get the same CloudWatch capabilities, including Transaction Search, Amazon CloudWatch Application Signals, and Amazon CloudWatch Omni. Bearer token authentication for traces is available in all commercial AWS Regions where the AWS X-Ray OTLP traces endpoint is available. To learn more, see Setting up bearer token authentication for traces in the AWS X-Ray Developer Guide.
title: Amazon CloudWatch now supports API keys for OpenTelemetry traces

summary: WorkSpaces for AI agents now supports Linux and Windows 11 cloud desktops, in addition to Windows Server. You can run each AI agent on the operating system that its workflows and applications require. Your agents can then work in the same environments that your workforce already uses, without re-platforming. Linux desktops give agents full root access to the operating system where many developers already build, test, and automate agentic workflows. Agents can take on developer tasks, such as running builds, tests, and scripts, within the enterprise-grade security and governance controls you already rely on. Windows 11 desktops let agents work in the enterprise applications your teams depend on every day. Linux and Windows 11 desktops have the same security and governance controls as Windows Server desktops. These include network isolation, IAM-based access, and the compliance boundaries your organization already has in place. To get started operating AI agents on WorkSpaces, visit: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appstream2/latest/developerguide/agent-access.html .
title: Amazon WorkSpaces for AI agents now supports Linux and Windows 11 cloud desktops

summary: AWS Interconnect - last mile is now available in preview with Equinix. You can connect your infrastructure across Equinix's global network of 282 data centers worldwide to AWS in a few clicks. Interconnect - last mile gives you managed, private, and resilient connections to AWS, so you don't have to order cross-connects or configure routers. To set up in the AWS Management Console, choose an AWS Region, a bandwidth speed, a Direct Connect gateway, and your Equinix Fabric One project ID. AWS generates an activation key, which you enter in the Equinix Fabric One portal to complete the setup. You can also initiate the connection from the Equinix Fabric One portal. AWS and Equinix set up quad-redundant capacity in advance, across two locations and four separate links, with BGP peering, VLANs and ASNs configured for you. Every connection is built for maximum resilience and comes with a 99.99% availability SLA. Traffic between AWS and Equinix edge devices is encrypted with MACsec by default. During the preview, you can order 1 Gbps Interconnect - last mile connections at no charge to the US West (N. California) Region through the San Jose metro and to the US East (N. Virginia) Region through the Northern Virginia metro. When Interconnect - last mile with Equinix becomes generally available, you'll be able to scale bandwidth from 1 Gbps to 100 Gbps in the console. You can create connections using the console, the AWS CLI, or the API. Partners can integrate using the open API package
title: AWS announces AWS Interconnect - last mile preview with Equinix

summary: Amazon RDS for Oracle now lets you copy the option group associated with a DB snapshot when you copy that snapshot to another AWS Region. Amazon RDS for Oracle uses option groups to enable and configure features that make it simple to manage your databases. Option groups are specific to the AWS Region where you create them. Previously, customers wanting to replicate RDS backups that had option groups to a different AWS Region had to copy the snapshot without the option group and then recreate the option group in the target Region before restoring the snapshot. Now, you no longer need to separate the steps and can instead initiate the snapshot copy and specify the option group copy in the same request as the snapshot copy. The existing boolean parameter CopyOptionGroup on the CopyDBSnapshot API and CLI commands now also support cross-Region copy, along with cross-account copy. You can now copy options groups to the destination snapshot in the target AWS Region from the source snapshot by setting this parameter to true . This capability is available on Amazon RDS for Oracle in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, review the Amazon RDS API Documentation .
title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports copying option groups during cross-Region snapshot copy
